samples.summary: The text-box editor's `toggleList` exit change ships with no behavioral test
samples.evidence: The diff changes three parallel `toggleList` implementations to exit through `unlistedBlockType`: `view/editor.ts` (covered by `list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts` → 'toggleList round trip'), `view/text-editor.ts` (covered by 'keyboard bullet shortcut round trip'), and `view/text-box-editor.ts:1125` — which has no coverage. The only existing test touching it is `packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:327` ('exposes toggleList, indent, outdent'), which asserts `typeof api.toggleList === 'function'` and `expect(() => api.toggleList('unordered')).not.toThrow()` on a paragraph with no selection — it passes identically whether the exit produces a heading or a paragraph, so it is fake coverage for this change. Ironically the new test file's own comment says both toggleList paths 'must exit through unlistedBlockType or the keyboard path silently drifts', yet only two of the three named implementations are exercised.

samples.summary: 'plain-text serialization is unaffected' is a vacuous assertion
samples.evidence: The test asserts `serializeText({ blocks: [bulletedHeading] })).toContain('Quarterly results')`. `packages/docs/src/serialize/text.ts` never reads `headingLevel` at all (grep for `headingLevel` in src/serialize matches only markdown.ts:104), and `blockToText` falls through to `inlinesToText` for every non-table/rule/page-break type. The assertion therefore holds regardless of whether the remembered heading level is inert, so it contributes no coverage to the invariant the surrounding `describe` claims to prove ('a remembered heading level is inert while the block is a list item'). The markdown, blockStyleId and DOCX assertions in the same block are meaningful; this one is not.

samples.summary: No Yorkie-store test for the list-item → list-item (indent/outdent, bullet-kind switch) path keeping the remembered level in the tree
samples.evidence: MemDocStore has 'indenting a bulleted heading keeps the remembered level' (list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts) but the collaborative store's equivalent path — `keepHeadingLevel` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1396 combined with the `toRemove` computation at :1414 when `setBlockType(id,'list-item',{listLevel: n+1})` is called by `editor.ts` indent/outdent — has no test re-reading from the tree. The updated yorkie-doc-store.test.ts only covers heading → list-item and the explicit paragraph reset. A regression that dropped `headingLevel` on outdent/indent or on a bullet-kind switch would be caught only in the memory store lane.

samples.summary: `pastedHeadingLevel`'s 'a real heading keeps its level' branch is only tested on the tail block
samples.evidence: `pastedHeadingLevel` is applied to both the head block (text-editor.ts:3606) and the tail block (:3636). The tests cover: bulleted heading into non-empty head (dropped), bulleted heading into empty head (kept), bulleted heading into non-empty tail (dropped), and real heading into non-empty tail (kept). There is no case for a real `heading` block folded into a non-empty *head* block, so a head-side regression that returned `undefined` for real headings (leaving a heading with no level, the exact failure the function's doc comment warns about) would go unnoticed.
searchedFor: read the new paste describe block in list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts

samples.summary: The entry-parity test regex-scans source text instead of importing the entries
samples.evidence: `blockHelperExports` reads `src/index.ts` / `src/node.ts` with `readFileSync` and a `/export\s*\{([^}]*)\}\s*from\s*'([^']+)'/g` regex hardcoded to single quotes and the literal specifier `'./store/block-helpers.js'`. It never imports either entry, so it cannot detect a name that is listed but does not actually resolve at runtime, and a reformat to double quotes or a re-export routed through another barrel would make the node set (or both sets) silently stop matching. The `expect(browser.size).toBeGreaterThan(0)` guard keeps it from being fully vacuous, but an `await import('../../src/node.ts')` check on the specific symbol would test the property the header comment claims (import-time failure under the Node entry).

finding.summary: The text-box editor's `toggleList` exit change ships with no behavioral test
finding.evidence: The diff changes three parallel `toggleList` implementations to exit through `unlistedBlockType`: `view/editor.ts` (covered by `list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts` → 'toggleList round trip'), `view/text-editor.ts` (covered by 'keyboard bullet shortcut round trip'), and `view/text-box-editor.ts:1125` — which has no coverage. The only existing test touching it is `packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:327` ('exposes toggleList, indent, outdent'), which asserts `typeof api.toggleList === 'function'` and `expect(() => api.toggleList('unordered')).not.toThrow()` on a paragraph with no selection — it passes identically whether the exit produces a heading or a paragraph, so it is fake coverage for this change. Ironically the new test file's own comment says both toggleList paths 'must exit through unlistedBlockType or the keyboard path silently drifts', yet only two of the three named implementations are exercised.

verdict.reason: The docs text-box editor's toggleList genuinely exits through unlistedBlockType (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1125), the same change made in view/editor.ts:2870 and view/text-editor.ts:2191. The new regression suite packages/docs/test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts exercises only the other two: 'toggleList round trip' (lines 276-335) drives EditorAPI via initialize() from src/view/editor.js, and 'keyboard bullet shortcut round trip' (lines 343-409) drives TextEditor via keydown on the mounted textarea. Neither mounts a text box. A repo-wide grep for toggleList/unlistedBlockType shows the only test invoking the docs text-box API is packages/docs/test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:327-337, which asserts typeof api.toggleList === 'function' and that api.toggleList('unordered') does not throw on an empty freshly-mounted paragraph — that passes identically whether the exit yields a heading or a paragraph, so it cannot fail if the exit regresses to hardcoded 'paragraph'. I searched wide for indirect coverage: the other docs text-box tests (text-box-composing, text-box-link-trailing-edge, text-box-edit-link-in-place) never touch lists; every slides test that mentions toggleList supplies it as a stub (e.g. packages/slides/test/view/editor/text-box-editor.test.ts:90, editor.test.ts:1275) and packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:625-627 merely re-delegates; every frontend toolbar test mocks it with vi.fn() (text-format-toggles.test.ts:47, toolbar-focus.test.ts:48, mobile-text-toggles.test.ts:67, text-edit-section.test.ts:33); there is no e2e directory. No test anywhere asserts a headingLevel survives a text-box bullet on/off round trip. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a behavior change shipped with only a vacuous smoke assertion as its coverage — major.
